Independent distance and row/column analysis of K₃□C₃
correctness.rationale: An MMD pair can only be strongly resolved by an endpoint. Conversely, a geodesic through a given pair can be extended at its ends until both endpoints are MMD, and either selected endpoint then strongly resolves the original pair. In the Cartesian product maximality separates by coordinate, so the MMD graph is the direct product of K_q with the antipodal matching or the odd step cycle. The even components are crowns. Their independent sets lie on one side (empty counted once) or are one of the q cross-matched pairs, giving 2(1+t)^q−1+qt² per component. For odd n, adjacent occupied layers must be identical singletons. Aggregating all size-at-least-two layer states by their common neighbors and weight h_q leaves a weighted transfer matrix on empty, q singleton colors and heavy. On the uniform singleton coordinates it restricts to B_q; on the q−1 color differences it acts as t, giving the trace term and its correction. Complementation produces the asserted cover polynomials. In the odd cycles with an empty layer, a singleton run of length ℓ≥2 is improved by full alternating layers, since q⌈ℓ/2⌉>ℓ; isolated full layers yield q⌊n/2⌋, while no empty layer gives n. The only tie is q=n=3. For even n one vertex per component forces its chosen side. In odd n≥5 one vertex cannot force by rotation, and choosing both layers of the unique adjacent pair in the minimum cover forces it: after deleting that pair the remaining odd path has a unique independent set of maximum size. For n=3, q>3, two retained layers distinguish the basis. In K₃□C₃ the distance-2 pairs are precisely those differing in both coordinates; any two vertices fit both some two-layer and some two-color basis. Three vertices in two retained layers using all colors force that two-layer basis, with the dual construction for a two-color basis. This direct boundary check confirms six bases of size six and forcing number three.
residual_risks: The recorded nine-instance regression is finite corroboration and was not rerun; the proof covers all parameter values.
Forcing is relative to other minimum-cardinality bases, not other inclusion-minimal or arbitrary strong resolving sets.

evidence: Corollary 8(d) gives the even scalar qn/2. Corollary 15(d) gives min(q(r+1),(2r+1)(q−1)) for n=2r+1, equal to q(r+1) for q≥3. The minimal-solution enumeration theorem produces inclusion-wise minimal sets; the forcing literature gives n/2 and 2 for single cycles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Scalar dimension does not enumerate bases or all sets. A general algorithm listing minimal solutions is not a closed all-set evaluation or a classification of forcing. The cycle forcing values do not determine the product, notably at q=n=3.

evidence: Known conversion is exact but leaves the family-specific independent-set count to be evaluated. The close same-graph topology result computes homotopy invariants; the same-graph independent-domination result counts configurations minimizing size within maximal independent sets.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The odd trace requires distinguishing same-color singleton runs from transitions through empty layers; the q−1 color modes cannot be obtained from a scalar optimum. Maximum support tie and product forcing require analysis of the entire basis family. The even enumerator is an elementary crown count; the support for distinct value is the full parity-dependent result and rigidity, not the reduction alone.

evidence: The actual equivalent enumerator is the ordinary independence polynomial of the MMD graph: a union of crowns for even n and K_q × C_n for odd n. Theorem 3 supplies the equivalence but not its all-coefficient evaluation. The closest catalogue match 2189c58cd95e gives a top-homology rotation character for cycle lengths 3r.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A matching full independence-polynomial formula would count as coverage under z^{qn}I(z⁻¹). A homotopy type or a character of a homology group is not the size distribution of faces.

originality.rationale: The standard MMD/vertex-cover equivalence, product reduction and the scalar strong metric dimension are already established and are credited, not passed as novel. The distinct supported claim is the evaluated all-set polynomial and the associated exhaustive basis and forcing classification. The inspected comparisons do not state that result or mechanically imply it from exact enumerator or basis data for the same product.
residual_risks: An unexamined exact independence polynomial for K_q × C_n would give material coverage. The focused external search was uninformative and is not evidence of absence; the decision rests on the inspected analogous and same-graph results.
The already-known scalar dimension is excluded from the novelty decision.

value.rationale: Clique–cycle products are natural finite metric graphs. The full cardinality distribution gives information the known optimum and minimal-solution algorithms do not. The parity-dependent component/trace evaluation exposes the role of singleton colors and the exceptional tie at the smallest product; the basis census and exact witness sizes determine when a basis can be specified from a small subset. This is a useful exact invariant and classified boundary, not merely a recalculation of strong metric dimension.
residual_risks: The claim does not cover K₂ or other Cartesian factors and is assessed only for basis-relative forcing.
